nom: Murad Superactive Brightening Moisturizer SPF 50 with Vitamin C

segments.dry: Reviewers with dry skin are split: several say the formula isn't quite rich enough on its own for very dry skin and pair it with a separate moisturizer, while one reviewer with dry skin found this thicker formula sufficient to skip an additional moisturizer entirely.
segments.oily: Oily-skin reviewers are the most likely to dissent, with one saying it amplified her oily shine within a couple of hours, especially under makeup, and wasn't right for her, and another with oily skin calling it better suited to winter since it feels like too much in summer.
segments.combination: Combination-skin reviewers are mostly positive, saying it addresses their dry, dull patches while brightening and keeping them hydrated all day, though one notes it feels a bit oily right on application.
segments.sensitive: Sensitive-skin reviewers, including one testing it six weeks after CO2 laser treatment, report no burning or irritation even with daily reapplication; one caution is that it does carry a light fragrance worth noting if you're sensitive to scent.

concerns.dehydration: Most reviewers say the moisturizer keeps their skin hydrated all day without feeling heavy; the dissent comes mostly from dry-skin reviewers, several of whom say it isn't rich enough on its own and pair it with a separate moisturizer, and one who found the reformulated version less hydrating than the previous one and says it can dry out skin without an extra moisturizer underneath.
concerns.redness: Two reviewers report a severe reaction to the reformulated version — one broke out in hives with facial swelling and another developed large rashes within the first day — both contrasting it unfavorably with the previous formula; most other reviewers, including one testing it after laser treatment, report no redness or irritation at all.
concerns.spots: Most reviewers who mention dark spots or discoloration report gradual fading and a brighter, more even tone with regular use, some noticing a difference within days and others over weeks; one reviewer says she personally did not notice any change in her skin despite otherwise liking the product.
concerns.blemishes: Most reviewers report the moisturizer does not cause breakouts and call it non-comedogenic; the dissent includes two reviewers who say the reformulated version broke their face out, one of whom found the SPF 50 version too thick and went back to the SPF 30.
concerns.oiliness: Most reviewers, including several with combination skin, say the formula absorbs without a greasy or oily feel; the dissent comes specifically from oily-skin reviewers, one of whom says it amplified her oily shine within a couple of hours, especially under makeup, and wasn't for her skin.

aspects.libelle: No white cast on a range of skin tones
Layers well under makeup without pilling
Pump can be awkward or hard to fully empty

extraits.texte: The new formula breaks my face out! I have used the prior formula for years and I am so disappointed with this change. I never had any issues with the prior formula and this one keeps breaking my face out. Very, very disappointed.

extraits.titre: Got less skin damage from the sun
extraits.texte: Loved the old formula . Now my face has giant rashes all over it within the first day of use

extraits.titre: Good for dry skin, not so much for oily
extraits.texte: [I received this product in exchange for my honest review] Both my husband (dry skin) and I (oily skin) tried this sunscreen and had different experiences. My husband likes that it's light, non-greasy, has no white cast and is a moisturizer and sunscreen in one, though he notes as a moisturizer it's not quite occlusive enough for dry skin. I agree with his assessment, but the sunscreen amplifies the oily shine on my skin after a couple of hours, especially under makeup. I was surprised because it's not greasy at all when applied and feels really nice on the skin, but this is not the sunscreen for me.

[I received this product in exchange for my honest review] I've been using the Murad Superactive Moisturizer SPF 50 for a few weeks now, and it's quickly become a staple in my morning routine. The texture is lightweight yet deeply hydrating, which makes it perfect for layering under makeup or wearing on its own for a fresh, dewy finish. What stands out most is its brightening effect—within days, my skin tone looked more even, and some of the dullness I usually notice in the morning was noticeably improved. It gives a subtle glow without looking greasy. The SPF 50 is a major plus, offering solid protection without the heavy, chalky feel that many high-SPF products leave behind. My only small issue is that, while it's labeled "superactive," it may not be rich enough for very dry skin types on its own. But for normal to combination skin, it's a win. Bonus points for no white cast and no breakouts.
